title: Sleep-Based Tests (Wait-and-Check Flakiness)
pattern: A test that introduces hardcoded thread sleep delays as a heuristic to allow asynchronous operations or concurrent threads to finish execution before making assertions.
why_bad: It causes test flakiness and dramatic test suite slowdowns [515]. Under heavy load (e.g., in virtualized CI systems), the sleep time may be insufficient, causing arbitrary failures [223, 539]. Under normal conditions, it injects unnecessary idle time into the development cycle [515].
detection: Widespread use of `sleep()`, `setTimeout()`, or `nanosleep()` in test cases validating concurrent, asynchronous, or network operations [515].
counterexample: Explicit timing benchmark tests where system delays or latency are the direct subjects of study under controlled environments [356].
fix: Use active polling with a tight interval loop (microseconds) and a generous maximum fallback timeout, or leverage event-driven notifications (such as channels, future wakeups, or promise resolutions) [223, 515, 539].
source:
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Larger Testing: Driving out flakiness" (p. 306) [223]
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Testing Overview: Fast tests" (p. 224) [515]
*   *Understanding Software Dynamics*, "Nanosleep performance bug" (p. 297) [582]
